purpose: Give every existing lspeak caller (bench Stop hook, classifier, bench daemon dispatch, sable, prismis) a speech command that returns at once and never crashes, by moving synthesis into a long-lived local Kokoro-FastAPI service and making lspeak a small Go client that queues, plays in order, and writes -o files synchronously.
form: The lspeak repo becomes one Go module (go.mod, module github.com/nickpending/lspeak, BurntSushi/toml its only dependency) holding a single main package, replacing src/lspeak/ wholesale. Files: main.go parses argv by hand against the kept flag set (--, positional text joined with spaces, stdin when no args and stdin is not a tty, -o/--output, -v/--voice, -p/--provider kokoro|system, --no-cache and --cache-threshold <v> accepted as no-ops) and refuses everything else with exit 2 naming the flag, refusing --model and -p elevenlabs with a message that they were dropped. config.go reads ~/.config/lspeak/config.toml when present ([tts] provider and voice, [tts.pronunciation] in file order via toml.MetaData.Keys, an optional [kokoro] url defaulting to http://127.0.0.1:8880) and ignores the old [http] and [cache] tables; a missing file means provider kokoro, voice af_heart, no pronunciations. pronounce.go ports src/lspeak/providers/kokoro.py:79: each entry, in file order, rewrites whole-word case-sensitive occurrences to [word](/ipa/), using Unicode letter/digit/underscore boundary checks to match Python's \b, Kokoro only. synth.go holds the two providers: kokoro POSTs {model:kokoro,input,voice,response_format} to <url>/v1/audio/speech and returns the body (non-200 is an error naming status and body); system runs say -o <tmp>.aiff [-v voice only when -v was given] <text> then afconvert -f WAVE -d LEI16 into the target. Output mode (-o PATH) synthesizes in the calling process, writes to a temp file in PATH's directory and renames it onto PATH (resolved against the caller's cwd), prints 'Audio saved to PATH' only after the rename, and exits 0 only then; kokoro's response_format comes from PATH's extension (mp3/wav/opus/flac/aac, else wav). Speak mode (no -o) writes a JSON item {text,provider,voice} to ~/.local/state/lspeak/queue/.<unixnano>-<pid>.tmp, renames it to <unixnano>-<pid> (nanos zero-padded so name order is time order), starts os.Executable() again with LSPEAK_DRAIN=1 in its environment, Setsid and /dev/null stdio, and exits 0 without waiting. queue.go is the drainer: open ~/.local/state/lspeak/drain.lock, flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB or exit 0; loop: list the queue dir (skipping dotfiles), take the first name, read and remove it, synthesize and play it (kokoro: WAV to a temp file then afplay; system: say [-v voice] text), log any failure with the item's text to ~/.local/state/lspeak/lspeak.log, re-list; when empty, unlock, re-list once more and start over if anything arrived. install.sh builds with go build into ~/.local/bin/lspeak (replacing the uv-tool symlink), writes ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.lspeak.kokoro.plist (ProgramArguments ~/.local/share/kokoro-fastapi/.venv/bin/uvicorn api.src.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8880, WorkingDirectory ~/.local/share/kokoro-fastapi, the start-gpu_mac.sh environment with absolute paths, RunAtLoad, KeepAlive, ThrottleInterval 30, stdout/stderr under ~/.local/state/kokoro-fastapi/, shaped like ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.bench.daemon.plist), and reloads it with launchctl bootout then bootstrap gui/$UID. src/, tests/, pyproject.toml and uv.lock are deleted; README.md and docs/IDEA.md describe the Go client and service honestly.
commitments: The caller contract is preserved flag for flag: every invocation in bench tts.ts:83, classifier.ts:76, dispatch.ts:323, sable tts.ts:83 and prismis audio.py:152-164 runs unchanged.
Speak mode never waits on synthesis or playback, so the bench Stop hook pays only process start, a file write and a fork per sentence.
Exactly one drainer plays at a time and plays in enqueue order; the flock plus the post-unlock re-check means no item is stranded and no two callers overlap.
A queue item carries its provider and voice with its text, so -p and -v reach the drainer that plays it.
-o is synchronous and atomic: the file appears complete or not at all, relative paths land in the caller's cwd, and the success line is printed only after the write, which fixes issue #3.
No ML stack runs in the lspeak process; the only OpenMP-bearing process is the Kokoro-FastAPI service with its single libomp.
The Kokoro service is owned by lspeak's install.sh on this host only, bound to 127.0.0.1.
sacrifices: No semantic cache: every sentence is synthesized fresh (about 0.2 s warm per the brief).
Speak mode reports no error to its caller: a down service or failed item shows only in ~/.local/state/lspeak/lspeak.log.
Playback starts only after a whole sentence is synthesized; no streaming into the player.
ElevenLabs, --model, --file, --list-voices, --no-queue, --queue-status, --daemon-*, --download-models, --debug and the HTTP API are gone; momentum calls that pass --model will be refused.
Non-macOS hosts are unsupported (afplay, say, afconvert, launchd).
risk: If the drainer's lock/re-check logic is wrong, sentences either overlap (two afplays at once) or a sentence sits in the queue until the next call; both are caught by the back-to-back and concurrent-caller proofs. If Kokoro-FastAPI's normalizer ignores the [Rudy](/ɹˈudi/) markup, 'Rudy' is mispronounced, caught only by rudy's listen check. If the LaunchAgent is wrong the service never starts and every speak silently logs an error, which the TTFA proof exposes. If the flag parser refuses something a live caller sends, that caller loses speech; the caller-contract tests replay each caller's exact argv.
